column1: # Domain campaign manifest: code16k (renamed from code4k 2026-08-18 with the cap). Generated by scripts/gen_domain_manifest.py,
# then COMMITTED -- this file, not the generator, is the source of dispatch.
# Namespace: MANIFEST=configs/campaign_code.tsv CLAIM_DIR=.campaign_code
# (BATCH_TAG=code16k lives in the claim dir; run names become <arm>_s<seed>_code16k,
# so checkpoints and fingerprints never collide with the math campaign's.)
# Columns: wave machine arm seed [note] -- same schema as campaign.tsv.
# 2026-08-18 re-pin: the 4-GPU family moved from 3 boxes (j5d2/3/4) to 6
# (j5d2..j5d7). Free to move -- zero code16k checkpoints exist, so no run sits on
# either side of it. Reason is makespan, not preference: a 4-GPU row needs a
# width-4 box, so the family's concurrency is 2 lanes per pinned box. On 3 boxes
# that is 6 lanes for 21 rows = 4 waves, while the 102 pool rows finish in ONE
# (26 boxes x 4 lanes = 104 >= 102) -- the family alone would have set the
# campaign's end date. Six boxes is the balance point, not the maximum: family
# 2 waves, pool 2 waves (23 x 4 = 92 lanes for 102 rows), and they end together.
# Going wider makes it worse -- 11 boxes buys the family 1 wave but starves the
# pool to 72 lanes, so the makespan is 2 waves either way and 5 more boxes idle
# 2 GPUs per pool lane they later claim.
# Requires a Job C of at least 8 boxes: a pinned row has no fallback (campaign.sh
# matches $2==MACHINE || $2==any), so a row named for a box that never boots
# never runs.
# -- wave 1: the noise floor, one box on purpose ------------------------------
